digest.top_line: MDACC RNI after NAT in cN+ breast (N=1289): adjusted 10-yr LRR HR 0.497 (0.279-0.884), DR HR 0.731, but univariate LRR 9.4% vs 8.1%, P=.62.
digest.tldr: All five studies are breast, all retrospective or pooled, all asking who needs PMRT or RNI. After NAC, risk follows residual disease and biology: 5y LRR 4.1% with pCR vs 9.5% without, TNBC non-pCR 18.5%, CPS+EG spread 71% to 99%. Without NAC, age <45 with >25% N+ reached 58.0% 10-yr LRR±SDR without PMRT.

sites.intro: Five non-randomized datasets on selecting PMRT and RNI by risk. None randomized RT, so every RT effect estimate here carries confounding by indication.

studies.name: CPS+EG staging and local-regional recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
studies.tldr: 5-yr LRR-free survival spanned 71% to 99% across CPS+EG scores vs 86% to 97% by clinical or pathologic stage alone, in 1697 pts after NAC.

details.text: 🔍 Retrospective, single-institution (MD Anderson), N=1697 treated 1997-2005; median f/u 51 mo

details: 🔍 CPS+EG = clinical stage + post-NAC pathologic stage + ER-negative (1 pt) + nuclear grade 3 (1 pt); score 0-6
💊 NAC anthracycline- and/or taxane-based; pts given neoadjuvant trastuzumab excluded

details.text: 🔍 Local therapy after NAC (non-randomized, chosen by pt/surgeon/rad onc)
📊 5-yr LRR-free survival by CPS+EG score (Table 4)
📊 Crude LRR by local therapy (overall 6.5%, N=110)
📊 PMRT-indicated subgroup (cStage III or ypN+, N=1103): LRR-free by local therapy (Fig 2)

details: 📐 MVA: CPS+EG ≥3, ≥4 and ≥6 linked to higher LRR risk; mastectomy alone higher, PMRT marginally lower
⚠️ Table 5 HRs can't be reliably tied to rows in source; per-score HRs not quoted here
⚠️ Text says LRR-free was higher with mastectomy alone in CPS+EG ≥3, contradicting the MVA; direction unclear from source

details.text: ⚠️ Overall LRR given as 6.5% in Results but 6.1% in Discussion
⚠️ PMRT-omission inference rests on non-randomized comparisons with small cells (mastectomy alone N=72 in CPS+EG 0-2)
🔗 vs NSABP B-18/B-27: 10-yr LRR 10.3% BCT, 12.3% mastectomy; those trials gave no PMRT

verdict.rationale: Retrospective single-institution series; PMRT-omission claim rests on non-randomized, physician-selected local therapy with a P=0.73 null read as equivalence in small subgroups. Pre-trastuzumab cohort.
verdict.audience: Breast cancer after NAC, cStage III or ypN+, no neoadjuvant trastuzumab

studies.significance: In the PMRT-indicated subgroup (cStage III or ypN+), pts with CPS+EG 0-2 had no LRR-free difference across BCT, mastectomy alone and PMRT (P=0.73, N=358), while scores 3-6 separated (P=0.0006). ER status and grade add biology to the post-NAC PMRT decision beyond ypN status, but cell sizes are small and HER2+ pts given trastuzumab are absent.
studies.monday_clinic: In ER-positive or low-grade breast cancer with residual nodal disease after NAC and CPS+EG ≤2, this supports a discussion about the small absolute PMRT benefit; it does not extend to HER2+ pts treated with neoadjuvant trastuzumab.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Retrospective analysis of the two MD Anderson cohorts used to build and validate CPS+EG, **N=1697**, treated 1997-2005. Median follow-up **51 mo**. Local therapy was not randomized.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: All pts received NAC (anthracycline, taxane, or both). **Neoadjuvant trastuzumab excluded**, as were pts given preoperative RT or missing ER/grade. Median age 50.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: PMRT was routinely recommended for **clinical stage III, ypN+**, and select cT1-2N1 with high-risk features. Dose, fractionation and target volumes are not reported in the source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **LRR** = invasive recurrence in ipsilateral breast, chest wall or regional nodes, counted regardless of distant failure, measured from diagnosis.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: CPS+EG spread 5-yr LRR-free from **71% to 99%** vs **86% to 97%** for clinical or pathologic stage. In the PMRT-indicated subgroup, CPS+EG 0-2 showed **no difference by local therapy (P=0.73)**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Matches **NSABP B-18/B-27**, where clinical nodal status and pathologic response predicted LRR, but adds ER and grade, which neither B-18/B-27 nor the MD Anderson Prognostic Index included. NSABP B-51 is the randomized test of regional RT after nodal downstaging.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents pts receiving anthracycline/taxane NAC without trastuzumab, treated at a high-volume center in the 2000s. Does not represent HER2+ pts treated with neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy or modern multi-agent regimens.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: A null P=0.73 in a subgroup of 358 (72 with mastectomy alone) is underpowered for equivalence. The Results text contradicts the MVA on the direction of the mastectomy-alone effect, and the overall LRR rate differs between sections (6.5% vs 6.1%).

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: CPS+EG separates LRR risk better than anatomic stage alone, which supports adding biology to post-NAC local therapy decisions. It does not show that PMRT can be safely omitted. That claim needs randomized data.

studies.interpretation:
The defensible finding here is prognostic. A score built for disease-specific survival, adding ER status and nuclear grade to clinical and post-NAC pathologic stage, separates local-regional risk better than either stage alone. The CPS+EG range of 71% to 99% five-year LRR-free survival, against 86% to 97% for clinical or pathologic stage, is a real gain in discrimination. It agrees with what the NSABP B-18 and B-27 combined analysis found for clinical nodal status and pathologic response, and it extends that work and the MD Anderson Prognostic Index by adding tumor biology, which neither of those used.

The therapeutic claim is weaker, and readers should treat it that way. The suggestion that PMRT could be omitted for CPS+EG 0 to 2 in clinical stage III or ypN+ disease comes from a null comparison (P=0.73) across three non-randomized local therapy groups, one with only 72 mastectomy-alone pts. A non-significant log-rank test in a subgroup this size is absence of evidence, not evidence of equivalence. Local therapy was also chosen by the patient, surgeon and radiation oncologist, so the mastectomy-alone group in the low-score stratum was almost certainly selected for favorable features beyond the score. Confounding by indication runs in the direction that flatters omission.

Two internal inconsistencies should lower confidence further. The Results text says five-year LRR-free survival in CPS+EG 3 to 6 was higher with mastectomy alone, but the multivariable model reports higher LRR risk with mastectomy alone and marginally lower risk with PMRT. Both cannot be right. The direction in the multivariable model is the clinically plausible one, but a reader cannot check the curve from the source. The overall LRR rate also appears as 6.5% in one section and 6.1% in another. Neither error overturns the prognostic result, but both suggest the subgroup analysis was handled less carefully than the headline staging comparison.

The bigger problem for transfer to current practice is the era. The cohort excludes pts treated with neoadjuvant trastuzumab, and the authors themselves name this as the most important limitation. HER2+ disease responding to anti-HER2 therapy has a different LRR profile, and modern NAC for triple-negative and HER2+ disease produces pathologic response rates that change what a given ypN stage means. A score calibrated on anthracycline and taxane regimens from 1997 to 2005 may misclassify pts treated today, most likely by overstating risk in pts who respond well to current regimens.

For the radiation oncologist, the practical read is narrower than the authors' conclusion. CPS+EG is a reasonable way to name the low-biology, ER-positive or low-grade pt with residual nodal disease for whom the absolute LRR benefit of PMRT is probably small. That pt is a fair candidate for a shared-decision discussion, not a demonstrated omission candidate. The randomized test of regional RT after nodal downstaging, NSABP B-51, asks a related question in a different population (nodes cleared rather than residual) and cannot settle the residual-node scenario either. For this study's conclusion to be wrong, unmeasured selection in the mastectomy-alone group would need to explain the null result. Given how local therapy was assigned, that is the likeliest explanation.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: In cStage III or ypN+ disease after NAC, CPS+EG 0-2 showed no LRR-free difference with or without PMRT (P=0.73, N=358). That points to ER and grade as a way to name lower-yield PMRT candidates, but the null comes from small, non-randomized cells in a pre-trastuzumab cohort.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Crude LRR was 8.1% after mastectomy alone vs 5.5% after BCT, and the MVA flags mastectomy alone as higher risk. CPS+EG ≥3 marks pts in whom choosing mastectomy without PMRT carries real local-regional risk after NAC.

open_questions: Does CPS+EG stratify LRR in HER2+ pts given neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy?
Is PMRT omission safe for low CPS+EG ypN+ disease in a randomized setting?

studies.name: Pooled analysis of nine neoadjuvant breast cancer trials: locoregional recurrence after NACT
studies.tldr: 5y LRR 4.1% with pCR vs 9.5% without (MV HR 3.33); TNBC non-pCR 18.5%. Surgery type not an independent predictor in 10,075 pts.

details.text: 🔍 Exploratory pooled IPD analysis, N=10,075, nine GBG/AGO-B neoadjuvant trials, 1998-2013

details: 🔍 Anthracycline/taxane-based NACT in all trials; cT4a-c and cT4d eligible in all but GeparDuo
📊 Median f/u 67 mo; LRR as first event, competing risks (Gray / Fine-Gray)
📊 Overall 5y LRR: BCS 7.8%, mastectomy 11.3%; mastectomy not significant on multivariate analysis

details.text: 📊 5y cumulative LRR by subtype, pCR vs non-pCR
📊 5y cumulative LRR by surgery type
📐 Independent LRR predictors within non-pCR pts
📊 After pCR, only cN+ trended toward LRR: HR 1.61 (95% CI 0.99-2.61), p=0.054

details: ⚠️ No patient-level adjuvant RT data; protocols only recommended RT per guidelines
⚠️ Surgery type likely confounded by selection: higher-risk pts steered to mastectomy
⚠️ Older trials gave HER2+ pts no anti-HER2 therapy; no post-neoadjuvant T-DM1 or capecitabine

verdict.rationale: Large pooled IPD from prospective trials, but exploratory and prognostic only. No patient-level RT data, so cannot inform RT benefit. Consistent with prior LRR-after-NACT series.
verdict.audience: Primary breast cancer, cT1-4d, after anthracycline/taxane NACT

studies.significance: The pCR split is where the RT read lives: LRR after pCR was 3.1-4.8% across all subtypes, while non-pCR HR-/HER2+ and TNBC reached 14.8% and 18.5%. Because RT delivery was not captured, these are LRR rates under guideline-directed RT, framing ypN0 de-escalation versus non-pCR TNBC as the highest-yield target for intensified locoregional therapy.
studies.monday_clinic: In a pt with residual disease after anthracycline/taxane NACT, particularly TNBC or HR-/HER2+, this supports treating locoregional risk as high regardless of BCS vs mastectomy; it does not establish whether RT changes that risk, since RT was not recorded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Exploratory pooled analysis of individual pt data from **nine prospective GBG/AGO-B neoadjuvant trials** (1998-2013), **N=10,075**. LRR as first event, with distant recurrence, second malignancy and death as competing events; pCR analyses used landmarks. Median follow-up 67 mo.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Primary invasive breast cancer, mostly ≥2 cm, with **cT4a-c and inflammatory cT4d** eligible in all trials except GeparDuo. 43.2% cN1, 44.3% G3; TNBC 25.8%, HR+/HER2- 45.8%. pCR (ypT0 ypN0) in 20.4%.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: All trials used **anthracycline/taxane-based NACT**. Anti-HER2 therapy varied by trial (trastuzumab, lapatinib, pertuzumab); GeparDuo, GeparTrio and PREPARE gave HER2+ pts **no anti-HER2 therapy**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Protocols recommended adjuvant RT per national and international guidelines, with regional nodal RT based mainly on nodal stage. **No patient-level RT data were available**, so RT is not an analyzable variable.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: On multivariate analysis, **age, cN, grade, subtype and pCR** were independent LRR predictors; **surgery type was not**. Non-pCR carried **MV HR 3.33 (2.60-4.28)** and TNBC **MV HR 2.72 (2.23-3.31)** vs HR+/HER2-.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The authors place this against the EBCTCG meta-analysis, which found higher local recurrence after NACT than adjuvant therapy in older trials, and the CPS+EG score as an alternative LRR stratifier. Response-adapted nodal RT after NACT is being tested prospectively in NSABP B-51, which this dataset cannot substitute for.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents pts with primary breast cancer, including locally advanced and inflammatory disease, after anthracycline/taxane NACT. Does not represent pts given modern post-neoadjuvant therapy (T-DM1, capecitabine) or populations where RT receipt is known.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: HER2+ estimates mix eras with and without anti-HER2 therapy, which the authors cite to explain the lower HR+/HER2+ LRR. gBRCA status and Ki-67 were incomplete. LRR was investigator-reported on case report forms.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: pCR largely erases the subtype gradient in LRR, while non-pCR TNBC and HR-/HER2+ concentrate the locoregional risk. What it does not settle is whether RT intensity or extent modifies that risk, since RT was not recorded.

studies.interpretation:
The value of this dataset is scale and denominator quality rather than any causal claim. Ten thousand pts drawn from prospective neoadjuvant trials, with protocol-defined pCR and investigator-reported LRR, gives cumulative incidence estimates by subtype and response that smaller single-institution series cannot stabilise. The headline structure is what most breast radiation oncologists already assume: response and biology dominate, and once pCR is reached the subtype gradient nearly disappears, with five-year LRR in the 3.1 to 4.8% range across all four subtypes. The divergence opens only in non-pCR pts, where TNBC reaches 18.5% and HR-/HER2+ 14.8%, against 5.9% for HR+/HER2-.

The RT reader has to hold one fact above all others: radiotherapy was not recorded at the patient level. The protocols recommended guideline-based RT, so these rates describe outcomes under contemporary practice of the era, presumably with most BCS pts and many node-positive mastectomy pts irradiated. That makes the numbers useful as a baseline risk map and useless as evidence about what RT adds or what omitting it costs. A 3.9% LRR after pCR and mastectomy does not tell you that PMRT can be dropped in ypN0 pts, because some unknown fraction of those pts received it. The question of response-adapted regional nodal RT belongs to NSABP B-51, and this analysis neither anticipates nor substitutes for that trial's answer.

The surgery-type finding deserves care. Crude LRR was higher after mastectomy, 11.3% vs 7.8%, but surgery type fell out on multivariate analysis and did not predict LRR within any subtype. The authors attribute this to selection, with higher-risk pts steered toward mastectomy, and that is the plausible reading. It is a reassurance about BCS after NACT rather than evidence that mastectomy is inferior, and it also suggests that whatever local therapy those mastectomy pts received was not fully offsetting their baseline risk, which is the authors' own argument for revisiting PMRT application after NACT.

Transferability to current practice is the main source of doubt. The trials span 1998 to 2013. HER2+ pts in GeparDuo, GeparTrio and PREPARE received no anti-HER2 therapy, and nobody received post-neoadjuvant T-DM1 or capecitabine, both of which the authors note improve outcomes in non-pCR disease with unreported LRR effect. The non-pCR HR-/HER2+ estimate is therefore probably an overestimate for a pt treated today, and the non-pCR TNBC estimate may also shrink with modern escalation, including immunotherapy, which these trials predate. The HR+/HER2- rates, under adjuvant endocrine therapy for at least five years, are likely the most transferable.

For this to mislead, the unmeasured RT distribution would need to differ systematically across the subgroups being compared, for example if non-pCR TNBC pts were less often irradiated. That seems unlikely given guideline-driven indications, but it cannot be excluded. The practical use is as a counselling and trial-eligibility reference: non-pCR TNBC and HR-/HER2+ define the population where intensified locoregional strategies are worth testing, and pCR identifies the group where de-escalation trials are reasonable to pursue.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: LRR after pCR stayed 3.1-4.8% across subtypes, versus 18.5% in non-pCR TNBC and 20.4% for TNBC after mastectomy. RT use was not recorded per pt, so this is risk stratification under guideline RT, not RT efficacy; it supports response-adapted thinking about PMRT and nodal RT after NACT.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Non-pCR TNBC (18.5%) and HR-/HER2+ (14.8%) carry the highest LRR risk, and these trials predate post-neoadjuvant T-DM1 or capecitabine, whose LRR impact the authors note is unreported. HER2+ pts in the earlier trials got no anti-HER2 therapy, which caps how well HER2+ estimates transfer.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Mastectomy carried higher crude 5y LRR (11.3% vs 7.8% BCS) but was not an independent predictor on multivariate analysis, and surgery type did not predict LRR within any subtype. Biology and pCR, not extent of breast surgery, drove LRR here, though selection toward mastectomy limits that read.

open_questions: Does RT extent modify LRR in non-pCR TNBC after NACT?
Can regional nodal RT be omitted after ypN0 conversion?
LRR impact of post-neoadjuvant T-DM1 or capecitabine

studies.name: Postmastectomy RT selection in T1-T2 N1-3 breast cancer (BC Cancer cohort)
studies.tldr: 10-yr LRR±SDR 15.9% without PMRT overall; 58.0% if age <45 with >25% nodes positive vs 10.8% if ≥45 with ≤25% positive.

details.text: 🔍 Retrospective population-based BCCA cohort, N=821 pT1-T2 N1-3, mastectomy + ALND, no PMRT, diagnosed 1989-1997

details: 🔍 296 pts who received RT excluded from the 1117 eligible, so the cohort is the RT-unselected remainder
💊 Systemic therapy in 94%: HT alone 57.1%, CHT alone 21.7%, both 15.1%; CHT mostly AC or CMF

details.text: 📊 10-yr KM ILRR 12.7%, LRR±SDR 15.9%; median f/u 7.7 yr
📐 Multivariate Cox: independent predictors of LRR
📊 Risk classification model, 10-yr KM LRR
📊 Pattern of regional failure (57 regional recurrences)

details: 📊 Grade 3, T2, and >1 positive node raised univariate risk but dropped out on multivariate analysis

details.text: 🔗 Baseline LRR well below the ~30% at 10 yr in DBCG 82b/82c no-PMRT arms

details: ⚠️ Pre-taxane, pre-trastuzumab era; HER2 status not analyzed
⚠️ RT benefit inferred from an assumed two-thirds relative reduction, not measured in this cohort

details.text: ⚠️ Small cells drive the top tier: the >50% LRR group is n=19

verdict.rationale: Retrospective no-PMRT cohort; RT benefit extrapolated from assumed relative reduction, not observed. Data-derived cutpoints, small top-risk cells, pre-taxane/pre-HER2 systemic therapy.
verdict.audience: pT1-T2 N1-3 breast, mastectomy + ALND, no PMRT, 1989-1997 era

studies.significance: Pattern of failure is the target-volume read: of 57 regional recurrences, 33% were clavicular and 3% internal mammary. That supports SCV coverage in a selected N1 patient over routine IMN coverage. Staging was ALND with a median of 10 nodes removed, so the >25% nodal-ratio cutpoint does not carry over to SLNB-only axillae.
studies.monday_clinic: In pT1-T2 N1-3 pts ≥45 with ≤25% of dissected nodes positive, 10-yr LRR±SDR without PMRT was 10.8%, which supports discussing omission; it does not extend to pts <45, those with >25% nodes positive, or SLNB-staged axillae.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Retrospective population-based cohort from the BCCA Breast Cancer Outcomes Unit, **N=821**, median follow-up **7.7 yr**. Cox multivariate analysis plus a stepwise risk classification model.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **pT1-T2 with 1-3 positive nodes**, modified radical mastectomy with axillary dissection, **no adjuvant RT**. Excluded pT3-T4, ≥4 nodes, M1, and the 296 pts who received RT.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Systemic therapy in **94%**. Chemotherapy was mostly AC (202) or CMF (91), and hormonal therapy was mostly tamoxifen (581).

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** isolated LRR and LRR±SDR (10-yr KM). **Secondary:** BCSS and OS, which were 71.3% and 58.2% at 10 yr.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Independent predictors were **age <45, >25% nodes positive, medial location, ER-negative**. In pts ≥45 with ≤25% nodes positive, tumor location and ER status further separated moderate risk (~20%) from low risk (<10%).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: No-PMRT LRR here sits below the **~30% at 10 yr** in DBCG 82b/82c, and close to the BCCA randomized trial (**16% at 10 yr**) and the systemic-therapy trial cohorts (**12-20%**). The authors attribute that spread to differences in axillary staging, systemic therapy, and selection.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents pT1-T2 N1-3 pts after mastectomy and full ALND, treated with 1990s AC/CMF and tamoxifen. Does not represent SLNB-only staging, HER2-directed or taxane-based therapy, or neoadjuvant-treated pts.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Cutpoints (age 45, 25% nodal ratio) were picked by examining significance, so they need external validation. Top-tier estimates rest on n=19, and HER2 status is absent.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The authors propose **<10% LRR as low risk (spare PMRT)** and **>30% as high risk (PMRT justified)**, with **15-20%** as the threshold for discussing PMRT. The model sorts pts by baseline risk but cannot show that PMRT benefit scales with it.

studies.interpretation:
This paper belongs to the generation of work that tried to settle the N1 PMRT question after the Danish and British Columbia randomized trials. Those trials showed a survival gain with PMRT in women receiving systemic therapy, but their no-RT arms carried locoregional failure rates that many centres did not recognise in their own patients. The authors frame the discrepancy explicitly. DBCG 82b and 82c reported roughly 30% LRR at 10 years without PMRT, while the systemic-therapy trial cohorts clustered at 12-20%. This series lands at the lower end, with a 15.9% LRR±SDR. That supports the long-standing suspicion that the Danish control arms were inflated by limited axillary dissection, which is why routine PMRT for every N1 patient never became universal.

The useful contribution is the stratification, not the pooled rate. Four factors held up independently: age under 45, more than a quarter of dissected nodes positive, medial location, and ER-negative disease. When stacked, they produce a spread from 10.8% in older women with a low nodal ratio to 58.0% in young women with a high one. Read against the authors' framework, the claim is that the absolute benefit of PMRT tracks the baseline risk. They assume a roughly two-thirds relative reduction and use the EBCTCG ratio of about one survival event saved per four locoregional events. That framework is reasonable, but the cohort never tests it. Nobody here received RT, so the benefit side of the argument is imported wholesale, and the paper is really a prognostic model wearing a predictive conclusion.

Several methodological choices should temper confidence. The age cutpoint was chosen because it gave the strongest univariate separation, and the classification breakpoints were picked by inspecting significance and subgroup size. Both practices overfit, and the model has no external validation set. The highest-risk cell holds 19 women, so its 58.0% estimate is fragile. Excluding the 296 patients who did receive RT makes the cohort a selected remainder: whatever drove clinicians to irradiate those women (likely adverse features) has been subtracted. That would bias the residual risk estimates downward, which is the opposite direction from the paper's argument and somewhat reassuring for its low-risk tier.

Transfer to current practice is the biggest problem. Every patient had a full axillary dissection with a median of 10 nodes removed. The nodal-ratio factor depends on that denominator and has no clean equivalent after sentinel node biopsy alone. Systemic therapy was AC, CMF, and tamoxifen, with no taxanes, no trastuzumab, no aromatase inhibitors, and no HER2 data. Modern systemic therapy likely lowers baseline LRR across the board, which would push more of this cohort's moderate-risk tier toward the authors' proposed omission threshold. SUPREMO was designed to answer this intermediate-risk question prospectively, and its results, rather than this model, are the better anchor for an omission discussion today.

The pattern of failure deserves more attention than it usually gets. Regional failures were mostly axillary despite full dissection, a third were clavicular, and internal mammary failures were rare. When PMRT is chosen for a selected N1 patient, that pattern supports supraclavicular coverage and gives little direct support for routine IMN treatment, though IMN failures are notoriously underdetected clinically. The paper is best used as a historical calibration of untreated risk, not as a selection tool for a contemporary SLNB-staged patient.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Clavicular sites made up 33% of regional failures and internal mammary 3%, which favors SCV coverage over routine IMN coverage when PMRT is chosen in N1 disease. The 10.8% LRR±SDR in pts ≥45 with ≤25% nodes positive defines an omission-discussion tier, though only for ALND-staged axillae.

open_questions: Does the nodal-ratio factor translate to SLNB-only staging?
Baseline LRR in N1 disease with modern taxane and HER2-directed therapy
External validation of the age 45 and 25% nodal-ratio cutpoints

studies.name: 21-Gene Recurrence Score and Locoregional Recurrence in Node-Positive Breast Cancer (SWOG 8814 analysis)
studies.tldr: 10-yr LRR 9.7% vs 16.5% for RS <18 vs ≥18 (P=.02) in postmenopausal ER/PR+ node-positive pts; signal confined to N1 after mastectomy alone.
details: 🔍 Retrospective translational cohort from phase 3 SWOG S8814 (tamoxifen or CAF-T arms), N=316 with RS
🔍 Postmenopausal, ER/PR+, node-positive; excluded mastectomy + RT (n=37) and BCS without RT (n=9)
📊 1° prespecified model (continuous RS) not significant: HR 1.14 per 10-point RS (95% CI 0.97-1.35), P=.11

details.text: 📊 10-yr actuarial LRR by RS category (low <18 vs intermediate/high ≥18)

details: 📊 By nodal burden, whole cohort: 10-yr LRR 9.0% (1-3 nodes) vs 24.4% (≥4), P=.002
⚠️ RS 18 cut point confirmed only in post hoc exploration; subset analyses not adjusted for multiplicity
⚠️ Mastectomy-alone cohort is physician-selected: higher-risk pts received PMRT and were excluded
⚠️ BCS + RT subgroup: only 6 events (2/29 vs 4/35), underpowered for RS comparison
🔗 vs NSABP B-28 (1-3 nodes, all chemo): 10-yr LRR 2.4% / 4.1% / 6.0% for low / intermediate / high RS
🔍 Median f/u 8.7 yr (IQR 7.0-10.2) in pts without LRR

verdict.rationale: Retrospective subset of SWOG S8814; prespecified continuous-RS model was null (P=.11), so the dichotomized signal and nodal subsets driving the PMRT read are exploratory.
verdict.audience: Postmenopausal ER/PR+ node-positive breast, mastectomy without PMRT

studies.significance: In N1 disease treated by mastectomy alone, 10-yr LRR was 1.5% with RS <18 vs 11.1% with RS ≥18 (P=.051), while ≥4 nodes ran 25.9% vs 27.0% regardless of RS. That splits the PMRT question: RS may help select N1 pts for omission (the TailorRT question), but gives no route to omit PMRT in N2+.
studies.monday_clinic: In a postmenopausal ER/PR+ N1 pt after mastectomy with an RS already in hand, a low score supports a TailorRT-style omission discussion on trial rather than off it; with ≥4 nodes the RS does not change the PMRT decision.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Retrospective translational analysis of the phase 3 **SWOG S8814** trial (enrolled 1989-1995), restricted to the tamoxifen-alone and CAF-T arms with banked tissue. RT use and LRR were abstracted retrospectively from trial records; reported per REMARK.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Postmenopausal, ER/PR-positive, node-positive** women; final cohort **N=316** after excluding mastectomy + RT (n=37), BCS without RT (n=9) and unknown surgery (n=5). 210 (66.5%) had 1-3 positive nodes; 124 (39.2%) received tamoxifen only.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** LRR (breast, chest wall, axillary, infraclavicular, supraclavicular or IMN), with RS modeled as a continuous linear term. **Secondary:** RS <18 vs ≥18, chosen owing to event numbers.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The prespecified continuous model was **not significant** (HR 1.14 per 10 points, P=.11). In MVA, **RS ≥18 (HR 2.36, P=.04)** and **≥4 nodes (HR 3.37, P=.001)** were independent; subset LRR rates in the table above.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Direction matches **NSABP B-28**, where RS was also independently associated with LRR, but B-28 N1 rates were low at every RS (2.4% / 4.1% / 6.0%). **MA.20** and **EORTC 22922** established a DFS benefit from regional nodal RT despite low LRR rates, which is why LRR risk alone may not settle omission.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents postmenopausal ER/PR+ pts with 1-3 positive nodes after mastectomy, treated with tamoxifen or anthracycline-based chemo then tamoxifen. Does not represent premenopausal, ER-negative, or modern taxane / aromatase inhibitor-treated pts, nor the BCS setting (6 events).

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The mastectomy-alone group is the **physician-selected lower-risk** stratum, since higher-risk pts got PMRT and were excluded, so the ≥4-node no-RT subset is unusual. No RT technique, target volume or dose data, and subset event counts are not reported, so the **1.5% N1 low-RS rate rests on few events**.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: RS behaves as a **prognostic marker for LRR** alongside nodal count, not a substitute for it. The authors' read: keep PMRT for pN2a at any RS and N1 with RS ≥18; enroll low-RS N1 pts on **TailorRT (MA.39)** rather than omitting off trial.

studies.interpretation:
The appeal of this analysis is that it asks a radiation question of a systemic-therapy trial whose design happened to leave a natural no-PMRT cohort behind. SWOG S8814 allowed PMRT at physician discretion, so a large share of mastectomy pts never received it, and their LRR becomes an estimate of the untreated locoregional risk that PMRT would be addressing. Read that way, the most useful number is not the headline dichotomy for the whole cohort but the split by nodal burden: in N1 pts after mastectomy alone, low RS sat at 1.5% versus 11.1% for RS 18 or higher, while with 4 or more nodes the RS made no difference (25.9% vs 27.0%). The assay appears to discriminate only where nodal burden has not already declared the risk.

Confidence should be tempered by the analysis hierarchy. The prespecified primary analysis, RS as a continuous term, did not reach significance. The positive result comes from the secondary dichotomized model, with the 18 cut point endorsed only by post hoc exploration, and the N1 mastectomy result itself is an unadjusted subset with a P value at the threshold. That combination is the classic shape of a finding that shrinks on replication. The exclusion logic adds a second layer: the higher-risk mastectomy pts were the ones offered PMRT and were removed, so the no-RT group is enriched for physician-judged favorable disease, and the 4-plus-node pts left in it are an atypical, selected minority. The near-identical 25.9% and 27.0% rates there still argue strongly against using RS to omit PMRT in N2 disease, because even a favorably selected group recurred at that rate.

Against NSABP B-28 the picture is consistent in direction but not in magnitude. B-28 also found RS independently associated with LRR, yet among its 1-3 node pts LRR stayed low at every RS, so in that cohort the absolute stakes of the RS split were small. B-28 differed in two ways that matter: no PMRT was permitted, and every pt received chemotherapy, whereas S8814 included a tamoxifen-alone arm. The higher N1 rate in RS 18 or higher pts here may partly reflect less effective systemic therapy, which is the second era problem: CAF and tamoxifen in a 1989-1995 cohort, before taxanes, aromatase inhibitors and modern axillary staging. Absolute LRR in a contemporary N1 pt is likely lower across the board, which narrows any RS-attributable difference.

The deeper reason this does not settle PMRT omission is that LRR is not the whole justification for nodal RT. MA.20 and EORTC 22922 both showed a DFS benefit from regional nodal irradiation in populations where LRR was already low, so a marker that predicts low LRR does not by itself predict that RT adds nothing. That is exactly the gap TailorRT was built to close, randomizing low-RS N1 pts. Until it reads out, the defensible use of this paper is narrower than its abstract: RS 18 or higher in N1 is a reason not to omit, and RS in N2 is not a reason to omit at all.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: In N1 disease after mastectomy alone, 10-yr LRR was 1.5% with RS <18 vs 11.1% with RS ≥18 (P=.051), while ≥4 nodes ran 25.9% vs 27.0% regardless of RS. RS may help select N1 pts for a PMRT omission trial, but gives no route to omit PMRT in N2+.

open_questions: Is PMRT omission safe in low-RS N1 disease?
Does RS predict LRR with modern endocrine and taxane therapy?
Does RS predict regional nodal RT DFS benefit, not just LRR?

studies.tldr: Adjusted 10-yr LRR HR 0.497 (0.279-0.884) and DR HR 0.731 with RNI after NAT in cN+ breast; univariate LRR 9.4% vs 8.1%, P=.62.
details: 🔍 Single-institution retrospective (MDACC), N=1289, cytologically confirmed node-positive stage II-III, NAT 1989-2007
🔍 RNI given in 1080/1289 (83.8%), at the discretion of the treating radiation oncologist
🔍 Median f/u 10.2 yr after definitive surgery

details.text: 📊 RNI effect: univariate 10-yr cumulative incidence vs multicovariate Cox

details: 📊 Without axillary pCR: adjusted LRR HR 0.476 (0.253-0.898), P=.02
⚠️ No multicovariate analysis for axillary pCR: too few LRR events. The B-51 question goes untested here
📊 HER2+ on trastuzumab: adjusted DR HR 0.237 (0.109-0.517), P=.0003

details.text: 📊 Axillary pCR 368/1289 (28.5%), prognostic on univariate analysis
subdetails: 10-yr LRR 9.7% no pCR vs 4.8% pCR, P=.006

details: 🔍 RT: median breast/CW 50 Gy/25 fx, then median boost 10 Gy/5 fx; multi-isocentric technique
⚠️ Control arm is mostly no RT: 142/209 (67.9%) of no-RNI pts got no RT at all
⚠️ Tangent field details unavailable, so high-tangent incidental nodal dose in the 'no RNI' group is unknown
⚠️ Univariate signal null or reversed for DR. The benefit appears only after adjustment, so confounding by indication is likely
⚠️ HER2+ pts without trastuzumab were excluded from all multicovariate models

verdict.rationale: Retrospective, RNI by physician discretion. The benefit appears only on adjusted analysis and is null on univariate. The comparator is mostly no RT, and it can't test RNI omission in ypN0.
verdict.audience: cN+ (cytology-proven) stage II-III breast, post-NAT, BCS or mastectomy + ALND

studies.significance: Residual nodal disease is where the adjusted LRR benefit holds (HR 0.476 without axillary pCR). In the ypN0 group, too few events allowed no model, so this supports RNI for ypN+ and says nothing on omission after nodal pCR. Two-thirds of the no-RNI group had no RT at all, so the HRs likely overstate RNI's increment over breast/chest wall RT.
studies.monday_clinic: In cN+ breast with residual axillary disease after NAT, this supports elective nodal coverage; it does not inform omitting RNI after conversion to ypN0, where the adjusted model was never fit.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Single-institution **retrospective** cohort, MD Anderson, NAT 1989-2007. Median follow-up **10.2 yr**. Competing-risk cumulative incidence (Gray test) plus multicovariate Cox models.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II-III breast cancer with **cytologically confirmed axillary metastases**, NAT, then BCS or mastectomy with ALND, **N=1289**. RNI pts were younger, with more LVSI, higher cT/cN/stage and less breast and axillary response.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Median breast/chest wall **50 Gy/25 fx**, median boost **10 Gy/5 fx**. RNI was defined as RT deliberately covering at least one regional basin. The institutional standard covered undissected axilla, SCV and IMN, with variable field design.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Univariate 10-yr LRR **9.4% vs 8.1%** (P=.62), with no difference within pCR strata. Adjusted LRR **HR 0.497** (0.279-0.884) and DR **HR 0.731** (0.541-0.988). **No DSS or OS effect.**

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: EORTC 22922 and MA.20 established LRR and DM reduction with RNI after adjuvant chemo, without a significant OS gain. This cohort maps that direction onto the NAT setting. NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304 is the randomized test of omission in cN1 converting to ypN0.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cN+ stage II-III breast after NAT and ALND, particularly with residual nodal disease. Does not represent ypN0 pts considering RNI omission, sentinel-only axillary staging, or modern HER2 dual blockade and post-NAT systemic escalation.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The control group is mostly **no RT at all** (142/209), so RNI is confounded with any RT. Tangent geometry is unknown, so incidental nodal dose in controls can't be excluded. HER2+ pts without trastuzumab were dropped from the models. The NAT era predates current regimens.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The univariate-to-adjusted reversal, with DR numerically higher with RNI before adjustment, shows how strongly treatment allocation tracked risk. The adjusted HRs are hypothesis-supporting at best. The HER2+/trastuzumab DR signal runs against older data suggesting HER2+ radioresistance and needs prospective confirmation.

studies.interpretation:
The headline finding here depends entirely on adjustment. Unadjusted, RNI did nothing for 10-year LRR (9.4% vs 8.1%), and distant recurrence was numerically worse in the RNI group (36.5% vs 31.3%). Only after the Cox model accounted for age, grade, LVSI, margin, residual breast disease, subtype and axillary response did RNI emerge as protective, at an LRR HR of 0.497 and a DR HR of 0.731. That pattern is what one expects when physicians gave nodal RT to the higher-risk pts, and the paper's own baseline table confirms it: the RNI group was younger, had more advanced cT and cN, and responded less well in breast and axilla. A model can only adjust for the covariates it captured. Confounding by indication in a cohort where 84% got the treatment, with the untreated minority selected for favorable features, rarely gets fully adjusted away. A reader should treat the adjusted HRs as a direction, not a magnitude.

The comparator matters more for an RT reader than the abstract suggests. Two-thirds of the no-RNI group received no radiation at all. The estimate is therefore closer to 'RT including nodes vs mostly no RT' than to the question we actually face in clinic, which is breast or chest wall RT with or without nodal fields. Tangent geometry was not recorded, so some of the remaining no-RNI pts may have had substantial incidental level I/II dose. Both features push the apparent RNI effect away from what the increment of nodal coverage alone would deliver.

Against EORTC 22922 and MA.20, which established that RNI after adjuvant chemotherapy lowers locoregional and distant recurrence without a clear OS gain, the direction here is concordant. The authors read it as evidence that the adjuvant-era benefit carries into the neoadjuvant setting. The more defensible read is narrower. Among pts with residual axillary disease, where the adjusted LRR HR of 0.476 held, the data fit with continuing to treat nodes, which is already standard. The decision clinicians actually want help with is omission after nodal pCR, and this cohort cannot answer it: the ypN0 group had too few events for a multivariable model, and the unadjusted pCR-stratified comparisons were null. That question belongs to NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304, which the authors themselves point to.

The HER2+ trastuzumab distant-recurrence HR of 0.237 is the most striking number and the most fragile one. It is a subgroup estimate from a cohort in which about half of HER2+ pts were treated before trastuzumab and were excluded from modelling. It also runs against earlier subtype analyses suggesting HER2+ disease derives smaller locoregional benefit from RT. A radiosensitizing interaction with trastuzumab is biologically plausible. An effect that large on distant disease from nodal fields alone should also prompt a search for residual imbalance before it is taken as biology.

What would make the study wrong? Unmeasured risk features that tracked RNI use, which is likely in a discretionary series. A control group whose benefit came from incidental tangent dose. And systemic therapy from 1989-2007 that differs enough from current regimens, including post-NAT escalation for residual disease, to change the baseline LRR risk RNI acts on. The nomogram is a useful way to put residual-risk factors in front of a pt. Its RNI term inherits the same confounding.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The adjusted LRR benefit holds with residual axillary disease (HR 0.476) but was never modelled in ypN0, so this supports RNI for ypN+ and leaves omission after nodal pCR to B-51. Most no-RNI pts (142/209) had no RT at all, so the HR overstates the nodal-field increment.

open_questions: Can RNI be safely omitted after cN+ to ypN0 conversion?
Does the HER2+ trastuzumab DR benefit persist with modern dual HER2 blockade?
RNI increment over breast/chest wall RT alone after NAT
